scope: Section 5 Eqs. (5.2)–(5.4). The explicit joint state has amplitude 1/√Q on each of the Q numerically distinct clock labels paired with its modular power. Its squared norm is one.
Section 5 uses the modular-power orbit. The natural modular data label depends only on t mod r; distinct residues below the exact order give distinct data basis labels.

Section 5 Eqs. (5.4)–(5.7). Multiplying the normalized inverse Fourier matrix by the modular-power state and summing over every data label gives the sum of squared period-class amplitudes. No register-outcome probability formula is assumed.
Sections 3 and 5. The primitive Q-th root gives orthogonal Fourier columns, and the explicitly normalized inverse Fourier matrix satisfies FᴴF=I for every positive Q.
Matrix trace and inverse Fourier unitarity imply that the actual clock marginal of the modular-power superposition has total probability one.
Section 5 after Eq. (5.13). ForShor’s good-outcome recovery statement transfers to the integer implementation of the bounded continued-fraction scan.

Section 5 Fourier order recovery. The ideal matrix experiment and executable decoder yield the true order r with probability at least (4/π²)φ(r)/r. The proof covers every integer Q>r² and specializes to the power-of-two clock N²≤Q<2N² for every valid modulus, including powers of two.
Section 5 selects a binary clock in the half-open interval N²≤Q<2N². The construction and its inequalities apply even when N² is already a power of two.
